moved.sentence: Parse at the boundary: convert untrusted input into a domain type exactly once; the parsed value *is* the proof.

judged.note: The rule keeps at SHOULD converting untrusted input into a domain type exactly once at the boundary, and that the parsed value is the proof.

moved.sentence: Don't thread raw strings and maps through the system and re-check them downstream.

judged.note: The rule keeps not threading raw strings and maps through the system and re-checking them downstream, as SHOULD NOT.

moved.sentence: Make illegal states unconstructable: model with the narrowest type that fits — sum types/enums for "one of", non-empty collections, bounded ranges, opaque/branded types — so a whole class of "this should never happen" branches disappears.

judged.note: The rule keeps at SHOULD modelling with the narrowest type that fits, with every listed type kind and the reason that never-happen branches disappear.

moved.sentence: Push the burden of proof upward, but no further: validate as early as the information is available, without forcing callers to prove things they cannot yet know.

judged.note: The rule keeps at SHOULD validating as early as the information is available without forcing callers to prove what they cannot yet know.
